headline: Georgia lawmaker Michelle Au urges cigarette tax rise to help fund Medicaid expansion
dek: Georgia state representative Michelle Au wrote on X that raising the state's cigarette tax to $1.92 per pack would raise $425 million in its first year, citing a Georgia DOR fiscal note.
body:
Dr. Michelle Au, a physician who represents the 50th District in the Georgia House of Representatives, argued on X that Georgia should modernise its cigarette tax to help pay for full Medicaid expansion.

Au wrote that Georgia has the second lowest cigarette tax in the nation. Its tax of 37 cents per pack was last updated in 2003, she said, compared with a national average excise tax of $2.06 per pack. She added that most states and the District of Columbia have higher taxes and have updated them several times since Georgia last did so.

She set out three arguments. First, she wrote that higher cigarette prices decrease smoking rates, with a particularly pronounced effect among younger smokers, who she said are more sensitive to price. Second, she said fewer smokers would lower state health costs linked to smoking. She noted that Medicaid patients smoke at twice the rate of the commercial payor population, and wrote that the state is currently subsidising preventable health costs of people who smoke. She described a higher tax as a reasonable "users fee".

Third, Au cited a Georgia Department of Revenue fiscal note requested by Senator Chuck Hufstetler, the Republican Chair of the Georgia Senate Finance Committee. According to Au, it shows that raising the state cigarette excise tax to $1.92 per pack would generate $425 million in the first year alone. She wrote that modernising the tax on vaping products would generate a further $97 million in that first year.

Au said the revenue would be enough to cover the cost of full Medicaid expansion and called for it to be reinvested in the public health system and in access to health coverage. She described the proposal as having strong bipartisan support and wrote that this is the year to act.
key_quote: Georgia has the second lowest cigarette tax in the nation.
